applies_why: This judge text calls D5 vs C5 UNDERDETERMINED and lists the almah/bethulah word-count cutting both ways as a reason, so it uses a two-sense verse as a ground for underdetermination.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8)
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand — reading one: a two-sense verse cannot be a ground for UNDERDETERMINED because both senses stand; reading two: cuts both ways is only a note that each side has lexical support and may still be weighed with other grounds.
why: The judge made UNDERDETERMINED partly because the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways, which treats a two-sense verse as open rather than letting both senses stand under K-S2.
